mainTopic: Where the עומר may come from: outside the Land, שביעית growth, last year's grain, and the source for requiring new grain.
overview: The גמרא first says that all opinions agree the עומר and שתי הלחם must come from grain of ארץ ישראל. The one exception is רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה, who holds that חדש outside the Land is forbidden by Torah law (״מושבותיכם״), so the עומר may come from there too. Next, a משנה says guards of ספיחין in שביעית are paid from Temple funds. רמי בר חמא asks how this fits with the rule that שביעית produce is for eating and not for burning. רב חסדא answers that the עומר is ״לדורותיכם״ and cannot be skipped. It also cannot come from last year's grain, because it must be כרמל, fresh, at the time it is offered. רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר then argue about the source for the rule against old grain: כרמל or ראשית קצירך. רבה brings a ברייתא proving the עומר is barley because it is the first new grain, and this ends in a תיובתא of רבי יוחנן. Finally the גמרא starts a משנה from ביכורים about the seven species, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Everyone agrees the עומר and שתי הלחם must come from the Land
steps.stepSummary: The disputing opinions argued about the 'new grain' requirement, but they all agree that the עומר and שתי הלחם must come from ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But about the Land, they do not argue: the עומר and the שתי הלחם from ארץ ישראל are valid, and from outside the Land they are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the earlier argument by pointing out one thing all sides agree on: these two offerings must be grown in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the opinions disagreed about the requirement that these offerings come from חדש, the new crop. This line narrows that argument. Whatever they held about חדש, they all accept the משנה's rule that חוצה לארץ grain is not valid for the עומר and שתי הלחם.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן, which permits the new crop
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות
They do not disagree
Outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: But regarding the Land, they do not disagree,
phrases.notes: 'The Land' here means grain grown in ארץ ישראל, as opposed to grain from abroad.

phrases.english: that the omer and the two loaves from the Land: yes,
from outside the Land: no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the previous discussion on the daf by limiting the scope of the earlier dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All opinions agree that the עומר and שתי הלחם are valid only from grain of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that the עומר must come only from the Land.
steps.simpleTranslation: In accordance with whom is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose view this agreement follows. This is a setup line, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'they do not disagree' sound as if everyone holds this rule. The גמרא checks whether some תנא holds otherwise, which would mean the rule is not universal.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with whom?

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule stated in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the עומר may not come from outside the Land.

steps.title: Not like רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה, who allows the עומר from abroad
steps.stepSummary: The rule does not follow רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה. He holds the עומר may come from outside the Land and reads ״כי תבאו אל הארץ״ as a matter of timing, not location.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not like this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה says the עומר may come from outside the Land. How does he explain 'When you come into the land'? It teaches that they were not obligated in the עומר before they entered the Land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule follows everyone except one תנא, רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה. He allows the עומר to be brought from grain grown outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ״כי תבאו אל הארץ״ seems to limit the עומר to the Land. רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה reads it differently. It tells us when the obligation began, which was once they entered the Land. It does not tell us where the grain must grow.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period
How do I explain (a פסוק that seems to contradict my view)?
'When you come into the land', the opening of the עומר passage

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not like this תנא' does not mean the rule is rejected. It means the rule follows everyone else, and רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה is the one dissenter.

phrases.english: It is not in accordance with this tanna,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
The omer may come from outside the Land,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה אֲנִי מְקַיֵּים ״כִּי תָבֹאוּ אֶל הָאָרֶץ״?
phrases.english: and how do I explain "When you come into the land"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:10

phrases.english: That they were not obligated in the omer
before they entered the Land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 by naming the dissenting תנא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule follows everyone except רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה, who allows the עומר from outside the Land and reads ״כי תבאו״ as timing.

steps.title: Why רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה allows the עומר from abroad
steps.stepSummary: He holds that חדש outside the Land is forbidden by Torah law, from ״מושבותיכם״. So ״כי תבאו״ is about the time of entry, and since the איסור applies abroad, the עומר may be brought from there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that new grain outside the Land is forbidden by Torah law, as it says 'from your dwellings', meaning anywhere you live. 'When you come' means the time of entering the Land. Since it is Torah law there, one may also offer the עומר from there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״מושבותיכם״ shows that the איסור of חדש applies wherever Jews live, even outside the Land. That forces ״כי תבאו״ to mean timing rather than location. Since grain abroad is bound by the Torah איסור, it is fitting that the עומר, which permits that grain, can also come from there.

keyTerms.meaning: Grain of the new crop, forbidden until the עומר is brought
From Torah law
Your dwellings, meaning anywhere you live
The time of entering the Land
They may indeed offer it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה ties two ideas together: if חדש outside the Land is forbidden by Torah law, then the עומר may come from outside the Land. Everyone else requires the עומר to come from ארץ ישראל.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a view on where the איסור of חדש applies leads directly to a view on where the עומר may come from.

phrases.english: And he holds that new grain outside the Land
is forbidden by Torah law,
as it is written: "From your dwellings,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:17

phrases.english: which implies any place where you dwell,
and "When you come" refers to the time of entering,
and since it is Torah law,
they may also offer it.
phrases.notes: He means they may bring the עומר itself from grain grown outside the Land.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָסָבַר חָדָשׁ בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the ברייתא quoted in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה, חדש outside the Land is forbidden by Torah law, so the עומר may also be brought from there.

steps.title: Guards of ספיחין in שביעית are paid from the Temple fund
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic with a משנה from שקלים: people who guard ספיחין in שביעית take their wages from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: guards of ספיחין in the Sabbatical year take their wages from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion by quoting a משנה from another מסכת. It is setting up an analysis of this ruling that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שביעית no one may plant, so the עומר and שתי הלחם must come from grain that grew on its own. Guards protect that grain, and the משנה says they are paid from the public Temple fund. The coming discussion will build on this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Grain that grew on its own, without being planted
The Sabbatical year, when the land must rest
The public Temple fund collected from the half-שקל
Guards of

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: 'There' is a משנה in מסכת שקלים, not our own מסכת.

phrases.english: The guards of aftergrowth in the Sabbatical year
take their wages from the collection of the chamber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, still connected to obtaining grain for the עומר and שתי הלחם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Guards of ספיחין in שביעית are paid from תרומת הלשכה.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא raises a contradiction about ספיחין in שביעית
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא points out a clash. The משנה implies the עומר is brought from שביעית growth, but a ברייתא says שביעית produce is for eating and not for burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא raised a contradiction to רב חסדא. We learned that guards of ספיחין in שביעית are paid from תרומת הלשכה. But a ברייתא teaches: "for eating" and not for burning.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא shows that two sources seem to clash. Paying the guards means the עומר comes from שביעית growth, but שביעית produce may not be burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying the guards from Temple funds only makes sense if the guarded grain will be used for the עומר. Part of the עומר is burned on the מזבח. Yet the פסוק says שביעית produce is "for eating," which the ברייתא reads as excluding burning.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises a contradiction between two sources
Their wages
"For eating, and not for burning": שביעית produce may be eaten but not burned

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama raised a contradiction to Rav Ḥisda:
We learned: the guards of aftergrowth in the Sabbatical Year
take their wages from the Temple chamber collection,
and contrast it with this: "for eating" and not for burning.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:6

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the implication of the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of the משנה in שקלים that the עומר is brought from שביעית growth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Part of the עומר is burned, and the ברייתא says שביעית produce may not be burned, so the עומר should not come from שביעית growth.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the תורה says the עומר is for all generations
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the Torah calls the עומר a law "for your generations." So it cannot be canceled in שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The Torah tells you "for your generations," and you say it should be canceled?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא defends the משנה. The עומר must be brought every year, שביעית included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא assumes that if שביעית grain cannot be used, the עומר would have to be skipped that year. Since the Torah says "for your generations," skipping it is not an option. So the עומר is brought even from שביעית grain.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Merciful One": the Torah, or ה׳ who gave it
"For your generations": the מצוה applies every year, forever
"It should be canceled," meaning the עומר would be skipped

phrases.english: He said to him: The Merciful One tells you "throughout your generations,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:14

phrases.english: and you say it should be canceled?

steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק overrides the objection: the עומר is required every year
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since שביעית produce may not be burned, the עומר would not come from that year's growth.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עומר must be brought in every generation, so it is brought from שביעית growth too.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: bring the עומר from last year's grain
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא says he never meant the עומר should be skipped. It could be brought from last year's grain instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Am I saying it should be canceled? Let him bring it from last year's grain!
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא pushes back. Nobody has to skip the עומר, because there is another source of grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain that grew in year six is not שביעית produce, so it may be burned. רב חסדא's reason ("don't cancel the עומר") no longer forces using שביעית grain. The challenge is back on the table.

keyTerms.meaning: Last year
"Let him bring"

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וּמִי קָאָמֵינָא אֲנָא תִּיבְטַל?!
phrases.english: He said to him: Am I saying it should be canceled?!
Let him bring it from last year's grain!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וּמִי קָאָמֵינָא אֲנָא תִּיבְטַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 7 by offering a way to bring the עומר without canceling it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the עומר would otherwise be canceled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Grain from last year is not שביעית produce, so the עומר can be brought without using שביעית grain and without canceling the מצוה.

steps.title: The עומר must be כרמל, fresh grain
steps.stepSummary: Last year's grain will not work, because the עומר must be כרמל, fresh soft grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: I need "כרמל," and that is missing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא rejects the suggestion to use last year's grain. Grain that has been growing that long is no longer fresh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah describes the עומר as כרמל, young soft grain. Grain that sprouted last year has grown too long to count as כרמל. Last year's crop cannot be used.

keyTerms.meaning: Fresh, soft, young grain
"I need" or "we require"
"It is not there" or "it is missing"

phrases.english: I require "fresh ear," and that is not present.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:14

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion to bring the עומר from last year's grain
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Last year's grain is not כרמל, the fresh grain the Torah requires.

steps.title: Use fresh grain harvested last year
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא tries again: take grain that was cut last year while it was still fresh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him bring it from last year's fresh grain?
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge comes back in a sharper form. If freshness is the problem, use grain that was harvested last year while it was still fresh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps the grain out of שביעית and seems to meet the כרמל requirement. The grain was fresh when it was cut. The question is whether that is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Fresh grain that was cut last year

phrases.english: But let him bring it from last year's fresh grain?
phrases.notes: He means grain cut last year while it was still young and soft.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gets around the rejection in step 9 by using grain that was fresh when harvested.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rejection that last year's grain is not כרמל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Grain cut fresh last year was כרמל, so it should satisfy the requirement without using שביעית produce.

steps.title: It must be כרמל at the time of offering
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק "כרמל תקריב" teaches that the grain must still be fresh when it is offered. Last year's harvest is no longer fresh.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "כרמל you shall bring." We need כרמל at the time of offering, and that is missing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא rejects the last suggestion with a פסוק. Last year's grain has dried out and is not fresh when it would be offered. So the עומר must come from the current crop, even in שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "כרמל" and "תקריב" (you shall bring) sit right next to each other. This teaches that the grain must be fresh at the moment it is offered, not just when it was cut. Grain stored for a year has turned hard, so only the current year's crop works.

keyTerms.meaning: "You shall bring (offer)"
At the time of offering

steps.whatToRemember: The עומר is brought from the current year's crop even in שביעית. The Torah says it is "for your generations," and it must be כרמל, fresh, at the moment it is offered. That is why Temple funds pay the guards of ספיחין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the משנה in שקלים. The עומר cannot be skipped and cannot come from old grain, so שביעית growth must be guarded for it.

phrases.english: The verse states: "Fresh ear, you shall bring,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:14

phrases.english: I require fresh grain at the time of offering, and that is not present.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion of step 10, closing the challenge that began in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion to use fresh grain harvested last year
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The grain must be כרמל at the moment it is offered, and last year's grain no longer is.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The עומר must come from the current crop even in שביעית, which supports the משנה about paying the guards of ספיחין.

steps.title: Two אמוראים give two sources for the new-crop rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns that the עומר cannot be from last year's grain from כרמל תקריב. רבי אלעזר learns it from ראשית קצירך, meaning the first of the harvest and not the end of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: רבי יוחנן says the source is "כרמל תקריב," you must offer fresh grain. רבי אלעזר says the source is "ראשית קצירך," the first of your harvest. That means the first of your harvest, and not the last of your harvest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a disagreement about which פסוק teaches the rule from the last steps: the עומר cannot come from last year's grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees on the rule itself. They only argue about where it comes from. רבי יוחנן uses the same פסוק as step 11, כרמל, meaning fresh grain. רבי אלעזר uses ראשית קצירך: the עומר must be the start of this year's harvest, while old grain is the tail end of last year's harvest.

keyTerms.meaning: "You shall offer fresh grain." The grain must still be soft and fresh.
"The first of your harvest." The עומר comes from the start of the new crop.
"The end of your harvest." Leftover grain from the previous year's crop.

steps.whyThisMatters: The next steps are an objection aimed at רבי יוחנן's source, כרמל. So it helps to remember which אמורא uses which פסוק.

phrases.english: It was said: Rabbi Yoḥanan says, "You shall offer fresh grain,"
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק from step 11, so רבי יוחנן agrees with that reasoning.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says, "The first of your harvest"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:10

phrases.english: the first of your harvest, and not the last of your harvest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rule just proven in step 11, that last year's grain is not allowed, and records a dispute about its source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both agree the עומר cannot come from last year's crop. רבי יוחנן learns it from כרמל, and רבי אלעזר learns it from ראשית קצירך.

steps.title: רבה begins an objection by quoting a ברייתא about the עומר
steps.stepSummary: רבה starts a challenge to רבי יוחנן. He quotes a ברייתא saying the פסוק מנחת ביכורים is about the עומר, which comes from barley. The ברייתא then asks how we know it is barley and not wheat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה raised an objection: "If you offer a מנחת ביכורים" means the פסוק is talking about the עומר offering. What grain does it come from? From barley. Do you say from barley, or maybe only from wheat?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה is setting up an objection against רבי יוחנן. He starts quoting a ברייתא, and the actual attack comes later, after the ברייתא is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says ויקרא 2:14, the פסוק that ends with the word כרמל, is about the עומר. It states the עומר is barley and then asks for a proof, since wheat is also possible. The next three steps give the proofs: one from רבי אליעזר and two from רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal offering of first grain. Here it means the עומר.
The עומר offering brought on the second day of פסח.
Barley
Wheat

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for רבה's question inside this ברייתא yet. Right now he is only quoting it. His actual point against רבי יוחנן comes after the ברייתא ends.

phrases.english: Rabbah raised an objection:
phrases.notes: His objection is against רבי יוחנן, who learned the rule from כרמל.

phrases.english: "And if you offer a meal offering of first grain"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:14

phrases.english: the verse is speaking about the omer meal offering.
From what does it come? From barley.
Do you say from barley,
or does it come only from wheat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts an attack on רבי יוחנן's source from step 12 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that the new-crop rule comes from כרמל תקריב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The attack is not spelled out yet. רבה is first quoting a ברייתא about the פסוק where כרמל appears, and his challenge will build on it.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר proves barley from the word אביב
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, רבי אליעזר compares the word אביב in the plague of hail in מצרים, where it means barley, to the אביב of the עומר. So the עומר is barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: the word "אביב" is used about מצרים, and the word "אביב" is used about the מצוה for all generations. In מצרים, "אביב" means barley. So the "אביב" for all generations also comes only from barley.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first proof in the ברייתא for its question, barley or wheat. רבי אליעזר links two פסוקים that use the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the hail plague, the פסוק says the barley was אביב, and the next פסוק says the wheat was not hit because it ripens later. Since the עומר פסוק also uses אביב, it must be talking about barley too.

keyTerms.meaning: Grain whose ears have formed but are not fully dried. Early-ripe grain.
For all generations. The מצוה that applies forever, not just in מצרים.
Learning a law by comparing the same word used in two places.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: "Aviv" is said about Egypt,
phrases.notes: שמות 9:31, the plague of hail: "the barley was אביב."

phrases.english: and "aviv" is said about the מצוה for all generations.
Just as the "aviv" said about Egypt is barley,
so too the "aviv" said for all generations
comes only from barley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from step 13 with a word comparison.
steps.raayaObject: That the עומר is brought from barley.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word אביב in שמות 9:31, which describes barley, compared with אביב in the עומר פסוק.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא proves barley from the pattern of offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא notes that an individual has obligatory offerings of both wheat and barley. The community has a wheat offering, so it should also have a barley one. If the עומר were wheat, the community would have no barley offering at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: We find that an individual brings his required offering from wheat, and also brings his required offering from barley. So the community too brings its required offering from wheat, and should also bring its required offering from barley. If you say the עומר is from wheat, we will not find any community offering from barley!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second proof in the ברייתא that the עומר is barley. רבי עקיבא uses a parallel between the individual and the community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An individual has both wheat and barley obligations. The barley one is, for example, the offering of a סוטה. The community has a wheat obligation, the שתי הלחם of שבועות. To keep the pattern matching, the community needs a barley obligation too, and the only candidate is the עומר.

keyTerms.meaning: An individual person
The community, all of the Jewish people together
His required offering, one he is obligated to bring
"We have found." Pointing to an existing case in the Torah.

steps.whatToRemember: So far the ברייתא has proven the עומר is barley in two ways: רבי אליעזר uses the word אביב, and רבי עקיבא uses the individual and community parallel. רבי עקיבא adds one more proof in the next step, and רבה's actual objection to רבי יוחנן comes after that.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: We find an individual
who brings his required offering from wheat,
and brings his required offering from barley,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף צִיבּוּר מֵבִיא חוֹבָתוֹ מִן הַחִיטִּין
phrases.english: and so too the community brings its required offering from wheat
and brings its required offering from barley.
phrases.notes: He means the community should also have a barley offering, so the pattern matches the individual.

phrases.english: If you say the omer is from wheat,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מָצִינוּ צִיבּוּר שֶׁמֵּבִיא חוֹבָתוֹ מִן הַשְּׂעוֹרִין!
phrases.english: we will not find a community that brings its required offering from barley!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָצִינוּ יָחִיד שֶׁמֵּבִיא חוֹבָתוֹ מִן הַחִיטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different proof for the same answer as רבי אליעזר in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That the עומר is brought from barley.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The parallel between the individual, who has wheat and barley obligations, and the community, which needs a barley obligation to match.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's second proof that the עומר is barley: the שתי הלחם must be 'first'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא argues that if the עומר were wheat, the שתי הלחם (which are wheat) would not be the first offering from the new crop. The תורה calls them 'ביכורים', so the עומר must be barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another proof: if you say the עומר comes from wheat, then the שתי הלחם would not be 'first fruits.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא, still inside the ברייתא, gives a second reason why the עומר must be barley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה calls the שתי הלחם of שבועות 'ביכורים', the first new offering. If the עומר of פסח were wheat, it would already be the first wheat offering, and the שתי הלחם could no longer be called 'first.' So the עומר must come from a different grain, barley.

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation, a second proof for the same point
First fruits; here it means the first offering from the new crop
"If you say": assumes the opposite view to show it doesn't work

phrases.english: Another explanation: if you say
that the עומר comes from wheat,
then the שתי הלחם would not be 'first fruits.'
phrases.notes: The תורה calls the שתי הלחם 'ביכורים' (במדבר 28:26).

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: אִם אַתָּה אוֹמֵר עוֹמֶר בָּא מִן הַחִיטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof from רבי עקיבא, alongside his proof in step 15, that the עומר is barley.
steps.raayaObject: That the עומר is brought from barley, not wheat
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק calling the שתי הלחם 'ביכורים' (במדבר 28:26), which only works if the עומר is not wheat

steps.title: The עומר is 'first' grain, so רבי יוחנן is refuted
steps.stepSummary: רבה finishes his challenge. The ברייתא treats the עומר as 'ביכורים', first grain. So last year's grain is invalid because it is not 'first.' That matches רבי אלעזר's source, and the גמרא declares a תיובתא against רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see that it is because of 'first fruits.' This is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה shows what the ברייתא proves, and the גמרא concludes that רבי יוחנן's view is refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole ברייתא is built on the idea that the עומר is 'ביכורים', the first of the new crop. So the reason last year's grain is not allowed is that it is not 'first.' That is רבי אלעזר's source (ראשית קצירך), not רבי יוחנן's source (כרמל, 'fresh'), so רבי יוחנן's view is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: Evidently; we see from here
Because of
A full refutation; the view being challenged is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that the עומר cannot come from last year's grain is based on the עומר being 'first' (ביכורים / ראשית קצירך), as רבי אלעזר said. רבי יוחנן's source from כרמל was rejected with a תיובתא.
steps.confusionAlert: The תיובתא does not reject the הלכה that last year's grain is invalid. Everyone agrees on that. It only rejects רבי יוחנן's reason, the פסוק he learned it from.
steps.whyThisMatters: It settles which פסוק is the true source for the rule against last year's grain, and closes the argument from step 12.

phrases.english: Evidently, it is because of 'first fruits.'
phrases.notes: This is רבה finishing his challenge from step 13. Last year's grain is invalid because the עומר must be 'first.'

phrases.english: This is a refutation.
phrases.notes: It is a refutation of רבי יוחנן, who learned the rule from כרמל instead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in steps 13-16 and applies it against רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's source for invalidating last year's grain (כרמל תקריב)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats the עומר as 'ביכורים', the first of the crop. That points to ראשית קצירך as the source, not freshness.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: תיובתא of רבי יוחנן. The rule against last year's grain comes from the עומר being 'first', as רבי אלעזר said.

steps.title: New topic: ביכורים come only from the seven species
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה from מסכת ביכורים. It says ביכורים may be brought only from the seven species that ארץ ישראל is praised for.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: one may bring ביכורים only from the seven species, and not...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a משנה from another מסכת. It is setting up a discussion that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה limits ביכורים to the seven species: wheat, barley, grapes, figs, pomegranates, olives and dates (דברים 8:8). The sentence continues with 'and not...', so the next part will list a further limit. The גמרא will then discuss it.

keyTerms.meaning: The seven species that ארץ ישראל is praised for in דברים 8:8
One brings
Except for; only from

phrases.english: We learned elsewhere: one may not bring first fruits
phrases.notes: 'Elsewhere' means a משנה in מסכת ביכורים.

phrases.english: except from the seven species, and not...
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: אֵין מְבִיאִין בִּיכּוּרִים חוּץ מִשִּׁבְעַת הַמִּינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the תיובתא closed the previous argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ביכורים may be brought only from the seven species (the משנה continues with more limits).
